subject: Post-call: PraxisPay cost anchors, batching levers & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxispay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PraxisPay cost anchors, batching levers & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: production inference spend is spiking during peak hours; current per-token cost (~$0.012/token equivalent) is above target and causing stress on your margin targets.
- Goal: get 30–45% reduction in per-request unit cost for the pilot workload while keeping p95 latency <= 500ms for session flows. Procurement wants clear budget gating by end of month.

Key levers we discussed
1) Batching (continuous + request coalescing) — expected savings: 20–30% depending on request size distribution.
2) KV/prefix caching for repeat sessions — good fit for your support chat flows; upside depends on cache hit rate (we’ll measure).
3) Model variant + quantization profile — can trade a small quality delta for another ~10–15% cost improvement.
4) Routing + burst policy — prioritize latency-sensitive routes, shift lower-priority work to cheaper capacity during peaks.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Hannah: I attached the spend snapshot you sent during the call and added a short pilot proposal (SOW draft to follow). Please confirm the sample window we should use for baseline (you suggested last 30 days). [Attachment: PraxisPay_Spend_Snapshot.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]
- Daniel / Leah: confirm budget band for pilot and procurement timeline. You mentioned ~ $80k–$120k over 3 months as flexible?
- Karthik & Marissa: can we size a 3-week pilot (dev + prod slices) that exercises batching and cache config with two quantization profiles? I recommend we include a single canary region and a fallback model for SLA guarantees.
- Schedule: propose kickoff next Wednesday 10:00am PT for configuration and measurement plan.

Success metrics (proposal)
- Cost: % reduction in cost per 1k API calls versus baseline
- Latency: p95 under 500ms for defined session flows
- Quality: automated evals on representative prompt set — no more than X% regression on top-1 intents (we’ll finalize threshold)

I’ll prepare the SOW draft and a narrower pilot scope after you confirm the baseline window and budget band.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com]
From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxispay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah@praxispay.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PraxisPay cost anchors, batching levers & next steps

Thanks Hannah — useful recap. Confirming a few items:

- Baseline window: please use June 1–30 (we have a stable traffic pattern there).
- Budget band: procurement gave us a green light to allocate up to $100k for a well-scoped 6–8 week pilot. That’s the number I’ll use when I push this to Finance.
- Priority: batching + prefix caching first. We can consider quantization if the quality tests look good.
- Procurement timeline: Leah is looping in our procurement mailbox — we need an initial SOW and a simple T&Cs sheet; approvals typically 2–3 weeks. If you have a standard procurement package, please send.

On the tradeoffs, the most important thing for us is predictable unit cost at scale — we can accept a modest latency increase on low-priority endpoints but not on user-facing chat.

Thanks — I’ll have Leah share the baseline telemetry export and an org-level contact for procurement.

—Daniel

Internal note — quick sizing thoughts after the call: 

- If baseline window is June and budget is ~$100k, we should recommend a 6-week pilot (2w config+dev + 4w measurement) to give caching warm-up time and observe peak behavior.
- Pilot scope:
  * 1 canary region (us-west) with continuous batching configured at 50–100ms batching window; measure per-route latency impact.
  * KV cache for session flows (start with 30% simulated hit target; measure actual).
  * Quant profile A (int8) on internal replica only as optional — safe rollback path to float32.
- Commercial levers: offer a one-time $10k credit toward pilot consumption if procurement needs aid to hit internal budget gates (this is doable but needs Hannah sign-off).

Marissa — can you draft a short measurement plan (KPIs + data collection) and a templated SOW that includes the credit as an optional line item? I’ll prepare the config steps for ops.

Karthik
